description_good_justification: The README opens with what the server does: one verify tool an agent calls before acting on data it did not produce, returning an evidence report: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README and the docs site explain how to get the server (npm), use it, and give feedback (GitHub issues); CONTRIBUTING explains how to contribute: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: The contribution process (issues, pull requests, checks, sign-off): https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
contribution_requirements_justification: Contribution requirements, including the design rules, coding style and tests, are in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
documentation_basics_justification: Requirements, installation for Claude Code and other MCP clients, and use without MCP: https://phun-ky.net/evidence-report-mcp/guide/
documentation_interface_justification: The report, every field and how the verdict is worked out (https://phun-ky.net/evidence-report-mcp/guide/report), each check (https://phun-ky.net/evidence-report-mcp/guide/checks/package), and the API reference generated from the source with TypeDoc (https://phun-ky.net/evidence-report-mcp/api/).
sites_https_justification: The repository (GitHub), the package (npm) and the docs site (GitHub Pages, https://phun-ky.net/evidence-report-mcp/) are all served over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone with a GitHub account: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/issues
english_justification: All documentation is in English, and reports and comments in English are accepted.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained, with releases and changes in November 2026: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/releases
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Every change is a public commit and pull request between releases, not only the releases themselves.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version, tagged as <version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning; a change that breaks the API or the EvidenceReport shape is a new major version: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged in git by the release workflow: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/tags
release_notes_justification: A CHANGELOG.md generated from conventional commits, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability in the published package. Such a fix would be listed in the release notes and a GitHub security advisory.
report_responses_justification: The maintainer answers bug reports in their GitHub issue. No one outside the project has filed a bug report yet, so none is unanswered.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered in their GitHub issue. No one outside the project has filed one yet, so none is unanswered.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests stay public and searchable on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, which is enabled, or by email: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Reports are acknowledged within 7 days; no vulnerability has been reported in the last 6 months: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
build_justification: npm run build compiles the TypeScript source to JavaScript, declarations and source maps with tsc: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development
build_floss_tools_justification: npm, Node.js and TypeScript are all FLOSS.
test_justification: A node:test suite run with npm test, a packaging check (npm run check:pack) that installs the packed package, imports it, runs the bin over stdio and runs the README's examples, and checks of the docs site: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
test_invocation_justification: npm test, the standard way to run tests in an npm project.
test_most_justification: The source is at 96.9% of lines and 100% of branches and functions; the uncovered lines are the bin's shebang and doc comments on type-only declarations. test:ci fails below 96% of lines or 100% of branches or functions, on every pull request.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The Check workflow lints, type-checks, tests with coverage, builds and packs every pull request and every push to main, on Node.js 24 and on 22.12.0: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
test_policy_justification: New behaviour must come with tests and bug fixes with a test that fails without them: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes came with tests: OSV severity parsing (c6ab427), the x-unit keyword (63c926a), C2PA checks with a fake c2patool (6715bf2), the README examples check (#48) and the docs site checks (#46).
tests_documented_added_justification: The tests policy is part of the instructions for contributing code: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
warnings_justification: TypeScript runs in strict mode, ESLint (typescript-eslint, stylistic and Prettier rules) on every file including Markdown, TypeDoc treats warnings as errors, and Ajv runs in strict schema mode.
warnings_fixed_justification: Lint has no errors and no warnings, TypeScript has no errors, and TypeDoc has no warnings.
warnings_strict_justification: TypeScript runs with strict: true, TypeDoc treats warnings as errors in CI, and lint errors fail the Check workflow.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer knows how to design secure software. The principles applied (fail-safe defaults, least privilege, complete mediation, minimal dependencies) and the threat model: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common errors for this kind of software and how they are countered: command and argument injection (no shell, absolute paths), server-side request forgery (one fixed URL), unchecked input (zod), resource use (timeouts and output limits) and supply chain: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#common-weaknesses-countered
crypto_published_justification: The server implements no cryptography. Its one network call, to OSV.dev, is HTTPS through Node.js's built-in fetch, which uses Node's TLS (OpenSSL) with its default certificate checks; C2PA signatures are checked by c2patool, which the user installs and configures: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_call_justification: The server implements no cryptography. Its one network call, to OSV.dev, is HTTPS through Node.js's built-in fetch, which uses Node's TLS (OpenSSL) with its default certificate checks; C2PA signatures are checked by c2patool, which the user installs and configures: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_floss_justification: The server implements no cryptography. Its one network call, to OSV.dev, is HTTPS through Node.js's built-in fetch, which uses Node's TLS (OpenSSL) with its default certificate checks; C2PA signatures are checked by c2patool, which the user installs and configures: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_keylength_justification: The server implements no cryptography. Its one network call, to OSV.dev, is HTTPS through Node.js's built-in fetch, which uses Node's TLS (OpenSSL) with its default certificate checks; C2PA signatures are checked by c2patool, which the user installs and configures: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations Key lengths are those of Node's TLS defaults.
crypto_working_justification: The server implements no cryptography. Its one network call, to OSV.dev, is HTTPS through Node.js's built-in fetch, which uses Node's TLS (OpenSSL) with its default certificate checks; C2PA signatures are checked by c2patool, which the user installs and configures: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations Node's TLS defaults exclude broken algorithms.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The server implements no cryptography. Its one network call, to OSV.dev, is HTTPS through Node.js's built-in fetch, which uses Node's TLS (OpenSSL) with its default certificate checks; C2PA signatures are checked by c2patool, which the user installs and configures: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations Node's TLS defaults exclude algorithms with known serious weaknesses.
crypto_pfs_justification: The server implements no cryptography. Its one network call, to OSV.dev, is HTTPS through Node.js's built-in fetch, which uses Node's TLS (OpenSSL) with its default certificate checks; C2PA signatures are checked by c2patool, which the user installs and configures: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations Node's TLS defaults negotiate key exchanges with forward secrecy (ECDHE, and TLS 1.3).
crypto_random_justification: The server generates no keys, nonces or other cryptographic random values.
delivery_mitm_justification: The package is delivered by npm over HTTPS with Sigstore-signed provenance, and the repository by GitHub over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are fetched over HTTP; npm verifies package integrity from the registry metadata over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The published package has no known vulnerabilities (npm audit --omit=dev runs before every release). Development-only advisories are fixed or accepted as the security policy describes: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been found in the published package.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are in the repository; GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) analyses every pull request and push to main, and ESLint with typescript-eslint runs on every pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL analyses the JavaScript and TypeScript code and the GitHub Actions workflows on every push to main and every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires its results, with no errors and no high or critical security alerts, before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open alerts; the ruleset blocks merging with a high or critical one.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or property-based testing yet: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#known-gaps
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: All software is TypeScript on Node.js, which is memory-safe; there is no C, C++ or other memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis runs yet. Input is validated with zod at the tool boundary, and the tests assert on reports, but there are no extra run-time assertions for a dynamic analysis to enable.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run yet, so it has found nothing to fix.
achieve_passing_justification: Not yet: the project is working towards the passing badge: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16929
dco_justification: Every commit must be signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin, checked on every pull request by the DCO app and required by the ruleset on main: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
governance_justification: The maintainer-led governance model and how decisions are made: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles, their responsibilities, and who holds them: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
access_continuity_justification: One maintainer holds the access to the repository and the npm package today. Releases use npm trusted publishing (no personal npm token) and the code is MIT-licensed, but no second person holds access yet: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
bus_factor_justification: The project has one maintainer, so the bus factor is 1: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/graphs/contributors
documentation_roadmap_justification: What the project plans to do, consider and not do until November 2027, linking the issues: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: The source files and what each does, the scripts and the docs site: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
documentation_security_justification: What users can and cannot rely on: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
documentation_quick_start_justification: Requirements, the one command to add it to Claude Code, and an example report: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/README.md#getting-started
documentation_current_justification: The API reference is generated from the source with TypeDoc on every docs build and deploy, CI fails on TypeDoc warnings (docs:check), the README examples run against the packed package in CI, and the docs site is checked page by page. Documentation defects are fixed as normal changes.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README shows the OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard badges: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The server has no user interface. Its docs site is checked in CI on every page with axe for WCAG 2.2 A and AA, in light and dark, and for sideways scrolling at 390, 768 and 1440 pixels (npm run check:site).
internationalization_justification: Reports are JSON for agents, but their summary, finding messages and notChecked entries are English text only; they are not localised.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub, npm and a static GitHub Pages site) store no passwords for external users.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Until 1.0 the newest release gets fixes and older ones are upgraded by moving to it; a change that breaks the API or the report shape is a new major version, and the release notes say what changed: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerabilities have been reported to the project; the repository has no security advisories.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: Reports are made privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email, then acknowledged within 7 days, assessed, fixed in a private GitHub security advisory, disclosed with a CVE where one applies, and credited: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
coding_standards_justification: Code follows the project ESLint configuration (eslint-config-phun-ky), Prettier and TypeScript in strict mode, and must pass lint, format:check, typecheck and docs:check: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The Check workflow runs ESLint, Prettier, the TypeScript compiler in strict mode and TypeDoc on every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires it to pass before merging.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries are built; the TypeScript compiler compiles TypeScript to JavaScript.
build_preserve_debug_justification: The build is not minified, ships source maps and declaration maps, and the TypeScript sources they point at are published with the package (checked by check:pack).
build_non_recursive_justification: npm run build runs tsc once with one configuration (tsconfig.build.json).
build_repeatable_justification: Dependencies are locked in package-lock.json and installed with npm ci; the published 0.2.0 tarball matched a pack of its tag file for file.
installation_common_justification: The server is installed and removed with npm (npm install evidence-report-mcp, npm uninstall evidence-report-mcp), or run without installing with npx.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is done entirely by npm, which honours its standard location settings (--prefix, npm_config_prefix, global or local). The package has no install scripts.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, npm ci, npm run build and npm test give the full development and test environment: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development
external_dependencies_justification: The dependencies are listed in package.json and locked in package-lock.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/package.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot checks npm dependencies and GitHub Actions weekly, dependency review checks every pull request, and npm audit runs before every release: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No third-party code is copied into the repository; all external components come from npm through package.json and the lockfile, and Dependabot opens update pull requests.
interfaces_current_justification: The code uses current interfaces: ES modules with an exports map, Node 24 in CI, TypeScript 6 in strict mode, the current MCP SDK, zod 4, and current GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Check workflow lints, type-checks, tests with coverage, builds, packs and installs the package, imports it, runs the bin over MCP stdio and the README examples, and builds and checks the docs site, on every pull request and push to main, reporting results as GitHub checks.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Four of the five bug fixes in the last six months came with a check that fails without them: C2PA findings (66f4b3c, with a test), the bin entry (a test in #34, and check:pack runs the bin), and the docs site layout and accessibility (check:site in #46).
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Line coverage of the source (tests excluded), measured with Node's built-in coverage on every CI run, is 96.9%, with 100% of branches and functions; test:ci fails below 96% of lines.
test_policy_mandated_justification: New behaviour must come with tests and bug fixes with a test that fails without them: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure design principles applied (fail-safe defaults, least privilege, economy of mechanism, complete mediation, open design, minimal dependencies): https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#secure-design-principles
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The server implements no cryptography. Its one network call, to OSV.dev, is HTTPS through Node.js's built-in fetch, which uses Node's TLS (OpenSSL) with its default certificate checks; C2PA signatures are checked by c2patool, which the user installs and configures: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations Algorithm choice is Node's.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The server stores no credentials or keys; c2patool trust anchors are files the user configures and can replace.
crypto_used_network_justification: The only network call, to OSV.dev, uses HTTPS: https://api.osv.dev/v1/query is fixed in the code.
crypto_tls12_justification: The OSV.dev call goes through Node.js fetch, whose TLS supports TLS 1.2 and 1.3; OSV.dev accepts TLS 1.2 and refuses 1.1.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Node.js fetch verifies TLS certificates by default, and the server does not turn that off.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: The certificate is verified as part of the TLS handshake, before the request with the package name and version is sent.
signed_releases_justification: Releases are published from GitHub Actions with npm trusted publishing and carry Sigstore-signed provenance; the signing identity comes from GitHub OIDC, not a key. Verification with npm audit signatures is documented: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated but not signed; releases are verified through npm provenance instead.
input_validation_justification: Every call of the verify tool is validated with zod against TargetSchema before any check runs; unknown kinds and missing or mistyped fields are rejected. Remaining gaps (schema size and depth) are listed: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#known-gaps
hardening_justification: Strict TypeScript, zod at the tool boundary, no shell for c2patool, timeouts and output limits on every outside call, one fixed network destination, read-only CI permissions with SHA-pinned Actions, CodeQL on every change, and a pack check before every release.
assurance_case_justification: What is protected, the threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, the common weaknesses countered and the known gaps: https://github.com/phun-ky/evidence-report-mcp/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
